      <content name="title"><span class="qt0">Child</span> Dental Health</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>

      <content name="altTitle">Oral Health, <span class="qt0">Child</span></content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Healthy teeth are important to your <span class="qt0">child</span>'s overall health. From the time your <span class="qt0">child</span> is born, there are things you can do to promote healthy teeth and prevent cavities. For babies, you should clean teeth with a soft, clean cloth or baby's toothbrush.  Avoid putting the baby to bed with a bottle and check teeth regularly for spots or stains.</p><p>For all children, you should:</p><ul><li>Start using a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste when they are two years old. You might start sooner, if a dentist or doctor suggests it.</li><li>Provide healthy foods and limit sweet snacks and drinks</li><li>Schedule regular dental check-ups </li></ul><p>Forming good habits at a young age can help your <span class="qt0">child</span> have healthy teeth for life. </p><p>NIH: National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research</p></content>

    <document rank="1" url="https://medlineplus.gov/childmentalhealth.html">
      <content name="title"><span class="qt0">Child</span> Mental Health</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Mental Health, <span class="qt0">Child</span></content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>It's important to recognize and treat mental illnesses in children early on.  Once mental illness develops, it becomes a regular part of your <span class="qt0">child</span>'s behavior. This makes it more difficult to treat.</p><p>But it's not always easy to know when your <span class="qt0">child</span> has a serious problem. Everyday stresses can cause changes in your <span class="qt0">child</span>'s behavior. For example, getting a new brother or sister or going to a new school may cause a <span class="qt0">child</span> to temporarily act out. Warning signs that it might be a more serious problem include:</p><ul><li>Problems in more than one setting (at school, at home, with peers)</li><li>Changes in appetite or sleep</li><li>Social withdrawal or fear of things he or she did not used to be not afraid of</li><li>Returning to behaviors more common in younger children, such as bedwetting</li><li>Signs of being upset, such as sadness or tearfulness</li><li>Signs of self-destructive behavior, such as head-banging or suddenly getting hurt often</li><li>Repeated thoughts of death</li></ul><p>To diagnose mental health problems, the doctor or mental health specialist looks at your <span class="qt0">child</span>'s signs and symptoms, medical history, and family history. Treatments include medicines and talk therapy.</p><p>NIH: National Institute of Mental Health</p></content>

    <document rank="2" url="https://medlineplus.gov/childnutrition.html">
      <content name="title"><span class="qt0">Child</span> Nutrition</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Nutrition, <span class="qt0">Child</span></content>
      <content name="altTitle">Teen Nutrition</content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>A healthy diet helps children grow and learn. It also helps prevent obesity and weight-related diseases, such as diabetes. To give your <span class="qt0">child</span> a nutritious diet:</p><ul><li>Make half of what is on your <span class="qt0">child</span>'s plate fruits and vegetables</li><li>Choose healthy sources of protein, such as lean meat, nuts, and eggs</li><li>Serve whole-grain breads and cereals because they are high in fiber. Reduce refined grains.</li><li>Broil, grill, or steam foods instead of frying them</li><li>Limit fast food and junk food</li><li>Offer water or milk instead of sugary fruit drinks and sodas</li></ul><p>Learn about your children's nutrient requirements. Some of them, such as the requirements for iron and calcium, change as your <span class="qt0">child</span> ages. </p><p>NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases</p></content>

    <document rank="3" url="https://medlineplus.gov/childsexualabuse.html">
      <content name="title"><span class="qt0">Child</span> Sexual Abuse</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle"><span class="qt0">Child</span> Molestation</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Sexual Abuse of Children</content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Sexual abuse is one form of <span class="qt0">child</span> abuse. It includes a wide range of actions between a <span class="qt0">child</span> and an adult or older <span class="qt0">child</span>. Often these involve body contact, but not always. Exposing one's genitals to children or pressuring them for sex is sexual abuse. Using a <span class="qt0">child</span> for pornography is also sexual abuse.</p><p>Most sexual abusers know the <span class="qt0">child</span> they abuse. They may be family friends, neighbors or babysitters. About one-third of abusers are related to the <span class="qt0">child</span>. Most abusers are men. If you think a <span class="qt0">child</span> may have been abused, it's important to report it.</p></content>

    <document rank="4" url="https://medlineplus.gov/childsafety.html">
      <content name="title"><span class="qt0">Child</span> Safety</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Safety, <span class="qt0">Child</span></content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>As parents, we want to keep our children safe from harm. Take steps to keep your children safe:</p><ul><li>Install the right <span class="qt0">child</span> safety seat in your car</li><li>Teach children how to cross the street safely</li><li>Make sure they wear the right gear and equipment for sports</li><li>Install and test smoke alarms </li><li>Store medicines, cleaners and other dangerous substances in locked cabinets</li><li>Babyproof your home</li><li>Don't leave small children unattended</li></ul></content>
